blocks: The Logseq user interface becomes messy-looking and sluggish when more than two levels of pages are embedded and are visible on a single page. It's okay if page MyPage has {{embed [[MyPage/MySubPage]]}}, and if MySubPage has {{embed [[MyPage/MySubPage/MySubSubPage]]}}, in it. It could be okay if there's only a single embed goes deeper and it's a very small page. But if the nesting goes deeper than that, it's usually a poor experience for the page viewer. As a convention, we permit embeds of L2 in L1 and L3 in L2, and use typical logseq wikilinks to L4.
A top-level Logseq/Entity/Book entity or a parent page of a Level 1 page has links to Logseq/Entity/Book/Section/Level 1 sections, not embeds.

Logseq/Entity/Book/Section/Level 1 has an embed of Logseq/Entity/Book/Section/Level 2, and Logseq/Entity/Book/Section/Level 2 has an embed of Logseq/Entity/Book/Section/Level 3. Beneath that, it uses links to Logseq/Entity/Book/Section/Level 4.
Use Block References deeper than Level 4
If a page has a section like 1.2.3.4.5, then 5 should be a heading on the level 4 page. If another page references 1.2.3.4.5, then a Logseq/Block/Id
Use Block References deeper than Level 4
A newly available child appears in its parent's embed list, and adjacent sibling pages link in both directions through prev:: and next:: once both exist.

Turn the source's paragraphs, bullets, callouts, figures, and tables into readable nested blocks. Preserve the information needed to use the material, not the PDF's line wrapping or table grid. Use > [[Note/Info]] or > [[Note/Warning]] for corresponding callouts.

Place a figure under its caption block. Represent the image with a Logseq/Entity/Asset/B2 page beneath its owning section; Logseq/Entity/Asset defines its page-derived filename. Embed the verified remote URL with the caption as alt text. Keep the full PDF outside the graph.

Replace page-number references with a link to the corresponding section when it exists and its identity is clear. Otherwise, name the destination in prose without a speculative link. Do not preserve a bare PDF page number as navigation.

Compare the extracted text and images against the source pages: heading order, callout scope, figure/caption pairing, and cross-references can be lost in PDF extraction. The imported page should read naturally in Logseq and nvim.
Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/02 Param Controls and its child Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/02 Param Controls/01 Knob Speed show a callout and nested section.
In this garden, Book Section Level 1 pages model the topmost numbered parts of a book or manual.
A Level 1 page sits directly under the work's root page. Its two-digit prefix follows the source's chapter order; its H1 retains the chapter number and full heading.
It contains the chapter's introductory material and embeds its Level 2 children in reading order. An empty chapter shell is unnecessary when the chapter has not been imported.
The shared section shape lives on Logseq/Entity/Book/Section. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc is an example.
In this garden, Book Section Level 2 pages model sections directly beneath a book's topmost part.
A Level 2 page sits under its Level 1 parent. Its two-digit prefix orders siblings within that parent; its H1 retains the source section number and heading when present.
It holds its own introductory material and embeds any Level 3 children at their source positions. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/02 Param Controls is an example.
The shared section shape lives on Logseq/Entity/Book/Section.
In this garden, Book Section Level 3 pages model sections directly beneath a Level 2 section.
A Level 3 page sits under its Level 2 parent. Its two-digit prefix orders siblings within that parent; its H1 retains the source subsection number and heading when present.
It holds its own content and embeds any Level 4 children at their source positions. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/02 Param Controls/01 Knob Speed is an example.
The shared section shape lives on Logseq/Entity/Book/Section.
In this garden, Book Section Level 4 pages model distinct headed sections directly beneath a Level 3 section.

A Level 4 page sits under its Level 3 parent. Its two-digit prefix orders siblings within that parent, even when the source leaves the heading unnumbered; its H1 retains the source heading and any source number.
A Level 4 page holds its own content. Smaller headings remain nested blocks within it unless the source hierarchy genuinely continues beyond this model.
The shared section shape lives on Logseq/Entity/Book/Section.
In this garden, Book User Guide pages model published instructions for using a particular item.
Place the guide at <Item>/UG, where <Item> is the page for the product or tool. One guide belongs to one item; search that namespace before creating another.
The guide page uses logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Book/User Guide]], [[Logseq/Entity/Book]]. It follows the shared book shape on Logseq/Entity/Book.
Place guide sections beneath <Item>/UG as Logseq/Entity/Book/Section instances. Their level, order, navigation, and page shape follow the level-specific section definitions.
The guide root links to its Level 1 sections in reading order; section content stays on the section pages.
Microfreak/UG contains the Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc section.

In this garden, Concept pages model understanding-oriented topics that follow the garden’s Diataxis-style shape (aligned with Diataxis/Concept / Diataxis/Explanation): paradigms, architectural lenses, and other “big ideas” explained rather than only defined.
When we treat something as a concept entity
Strong signals: the page’s purpose is understanding—what something is, why it matters, how it relates to neighboring ideas—not primarily a how-to, tutorial walkthrough, or lookup reference.
When we treat something as a concept entity
Good fit: programming paradigms, frameworks of thought, architectural patterns explained in prose.

Link shape: [[Topic/Concept/Idea]] or [[Topic/Explanation/Idea]] when the topic has enough pages to want the segment, as on Programming/Language/Concept/Object-Oriented and herdr/Explanation/Where Input Box Text Comes From.
A concept that is the topic takes the topic's own name, as cybernetics does.
Search for an existing page before creating a new concept entity.
Search order hints: exact title, alternate titles from frontmatter, normalized topic phrases, sibling pages in the same topic area.
Classify as: existing, similar (needs human judgment), new, or blocked.
On instances, set logseq-entity:: to a link to this entity-type page so backlinks list all concept entities.
Concept-specific tags may mirror the established Diataxis concept cluster when the page is new and that convention applies.
Shared frontmatter conventions live on Logseq/Frontmatter.
Use Logseq Flavored Markdown (bullets, headings as bullets, tab nesting, no blank lines between bullets).
Recommended sections (Diataxis explanation style): Overview, Context, Key Principles, Mechanism, Examples, Misconceptions. Adapt headings to the topic; not every section must be long.
First heading after frontmatter: H1 matching the page’s primary topic.
Concept stays first in logseq-entity::, and the other type follows it.

Logseq/Entity/Trade-Off — a concept that weighs choices against each other: logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Concept]], [[Logseq/Entity/Trade-Off]]. That page carries the page shape for the combination.
Logseq/Entity/Term/Acronym — a concept whose page name is an acronym, as on TAM.
Logseq/Entity/Field of Study — a concept that is also a discipline, as on cybernetics.
Diataxis framing in the graph: Diataxis/Explanation (aliases Diataxis/Concept). This type page is the operational template; those pages are the vocabulary of the framework.
Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/Explanation carries the quadrant's tag and writing guidance for concept pages.
Each Entity Definition page describes a type of real-world entity that may be tracked in a page Knowledge Garden page. Entity here means something roughly analagous

the garden tracks — each describes how to recognize, name, deduplicate, and shape instances of one kind of entity.

entity-proxy-source-properties:: lists property keys that an instance’s source garden controls, even when another entity definition gives those keys to the destination. This explicit source declaration takes precedence over entity-proxy-destination-properties::.

Re-sync updates, adds, or removes these properties to match the source. Removing a source property also removes the destination’s value. Protected tags:: and sync-owned proxy metadata cannot be assigned to the source through this declaration.
Logseq/Entity/Person, Logseq/Entity/Software/Project, Logseq/Entity/Book, and the other pages under the Logseq/Entity/ namespace.
What counts as an Entity Definition
A page under the Logseq/Entity/ namespace whose job is to define one entity type: what counts as an instance, what does not, how to name and deduplicate it, and what shape its instance pages take.
What counts as an Entity Definition
Not an Entity Definition: an instance page (an actual person, project, book, …), or Logseq/Entity itself, which is the general conceptual model rather than a single type.

Frontmatter — logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Definition]] marks the page as an entity definition, so this page collects a backlink to every entity type. Plural or contextual forms go in alias:: only when codekiln asks for them, per My/AI/Rule/Logseq/No Aliases Unless Asked. Never alter tags::.

H1 — a single bullet-wrapped heading in human-friendly Title Case, with abbreviations expanded and no namespace path: - # Software Plugin, - # Security Vulnerability, - # CLI Command. The page's namespace already carries it.

First line — one sentence directly under the H1 in the form In this garden, **<Name>** pages model <description>. These first lines read together as a self-describing index of the garden's entity types.

Keep shared conventions on Logseq/Frontmatter and Logseq/Pref rather than repeating them on each type page.

entity-tasks:: declares the reference pages needed to work with instances of this entity. The property is a comma-separated list of wikilinks in the definition's frontmatter; an absent property declares no companion tasks.

follows an instance's logseq-entity:: links, imports its entity definitions, and follows each definition's entity-tasks:: links. Task references declare their executable files and required task dependencies through the companion-file contract on .
Shared entity definitions and task dependencies are visited once per sync. Cyclic relationships are allowed and terminate after their pages have been visited.

A referenced entity definition with no source file is reported as a logical page. A declared companion task or task dependency requires a source reference page and its mapped implementation files; missing task content stops application.

entity-proxy-destination-properties:: names, as a comma-separated list of property keys, the properties on an instance that belong to the garden holding a of it rather than to the source page. Re-syncing that proxy keeps the destination's values for them. An absent property names none.
For example, names podcast-guid and podcast-published-at, which the publishing garden records.

Logseq/Entity is the general conceptual model — what an entity is and how any page is marked as one. This page is the entity type whose instances are the definition pages themselves, so the garden's set of entity types is queryable through its backlinks rather than kept as a hand-maintained list.
In this garden, Diataxis pages model documentation written for one reader need from the Diataxis framework: doing a task, learning a skill, looking something up, or understanding why.
Each child entity below extends this one. Pick the child by what the reader needs.
A page that serves one of the four needs. A topic that needs two of them gets two pages, each linking to the other.
Each child definition page says what its own instances look like and which of its siblings a near miss belongs to.
An instance carries its child entity alone: logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/How To]]. The child already says the page is a Diataxis page.
When the page is also another entity, that entity comes first and the Diataxis child follows it: logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/CLI/Command]], [[Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/How To]].
tags:: — a new page carries its child's tag from the table above, alongside its topic tags.
see-also:: — preferred over a ## Related section that only lists internal wikilinks.
Shared frontmatter conventions live on Logseq/Frontmatter.
Each child entity defines its own namespace, page shape and voice.
A page links out to its siblings when the reader needs them, so a how-to links to the explanation behind a step and leaves the explaining to that page.

In this garden, Diataxis Explanation pages model understanding-oriented writing: why something is the way it is, and how ideas fit together. They explain why and serve understanding, the reflective quadrant of Diataxis.
Choosing between the four children, marking an instance, see-also:: and shared frontmatter follow Logseq/Entity/Diataxis.
A page that gives background, weighs alternatives, or draws the connections between ideas, rather than instructing or cataloguing.
Not an instance: a page of steps — Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/How To or Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/Tutorial. A systematic description of a thing — Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/Reference.

This quadrant overlaps the entity system almost entirely: an explanation-shaped page in this garden is normally a concept instance, and Logseq/Entity/Concept governs its frontmatter, its naming, and its body sections.

Read Logseq/Entity/Concept first, then this page for the Diataxis vocabulary and the tag. Where the two differ, the Concept page wins on shape and this page wins on which quadrant the writing belongs to.
covers the narrower case of naming a thing rather than explaining it; a page can be both.
No namespace segment of its own — an explanation page is named for the idea it explains, wherever that idea naturally sits, per Logseq/Entity/Concept.
tags:: — new pages of this kind carry [[Diataxis/Concept]] (or [[Diataxis/Explanation]], the same cluster by alias).
Per Logseq/Entity/Concept. This entity adds no shape of its own.
Take a wider view than a task allows: the history, the alternatives that were not taken, the reasons behind a design.
Admit the disagreements. Explanation is the one quadrant where opinion belongs, provided it is marked as such.
Link out to the how-to, tutorial and reference pages rather than absorbing their jobs.
Diataxis/Explanation — the framework concept page this entity implements.

Logseq/Entity/Discussion — a Discussion page that weighs alternatives also carries this entity, after Discussion in its logseq-entity:: line. It takes its name, placement, shape and frontmatter from the Discussion definition, so an agent writing one leaves out the [[Diataxis/Concept]] tag that new Explanation pages otherwise carry.

In this garden, Diataxis How To pages model goal-oriented directions that walk a competent reader through solving one specific problem. They inform action and serve the application of a skill, the practical quadrant of Diataxis.
Choosing between the four children, marking an instance, see-also:: and shared frontmatter follow Logseq/Entity/Diataxis.
A page addressing a real-world task the reader already knows they want to accomplish, written as a sequence of steps rather than as teaching or description.

Not an instance: a page that teaches a skill the reader does not yet have — that is Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/Tutorial. A page that describes what something is — that is Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/Reference. A page that explains why — that is Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/Explanation.
Namespace pattern: Topic/Subtopic/How To/Specific Task, for example Diataxis/How To/Create a How To.
The title states plainly what the guide accomplishes. [[Programming/Python/How To/Set Up a Virtual Environment]] → pages/Programming___Python___How To___Set Up a Virtual Environment.md.
tags:: — new pages of this kind carry [[Diataxis/How To]] alongside whatever topic tags they already have.
## Overview — what the guide accomplishes, who it is for, when they would need it.
## Prerequisites — tools, knowledge or resources needed before starting.
## Steps — numbered ### 1. First Step headings, each with its details beneath. The sequence flows in a meaningful order.
## Troubleshooting — common failures and their fixes.
Omit a section rather than padding it.
Assume competence. The reader knows the goal; they need the route, not a lesson.
No digressions. Link out to explanation and reference pages instead of teaching inside the steps.
Practical over complete. Usability beats covering every possibility.
Language: conditional imperatives — If you want X, do Y. Open steps with an action verb — Install, Configure, Create. Present tense, active voice, concise.
When research is needed, add a ### Research block with findings, flag what is uncertain, and settle scope with the human before writing the steps out.
Diataxis/How To — the framework concept page this entity implements.

In this garden, Diataxis Reference pages model neutral technical descriptions of a thing and how it works — the source of truth a reader consults while working. They inform cognition and serve theoretical knowledge, the information quadrant of Diataxis.
Choosing between the four children, marking an instance, see-also:: and shared frontmatter follow Logseq/Entity/Diataxis.
A page led by the structure of what it describes rather than by a reader's task: specifications, parameters, components, constraints, laid out systematically.
Not an instance: a page that instructs — Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/How To or Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/Tutorial. A page that argues or gives background — Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/Explanation.

[[API/Endpoints/Ref/Authentication]] → pages/API___Endpoints___Ref___Authentication.md; [[Unicode/Block/Ref/Symbols for Legacy Computing]] → pages/Unicode___Block___Ref___Symbols for Legacy Computing.md.
tags:: — new pages of this kind carry [[Diataxis/Reference]] alongside their topic tags.
## Overview — a brief factual description, with the scope and its boundaries.
## Structure — how the reference is organized and what conventions it uses.
## Core Components — ### Component headings, each with a precise description, its specifications, its parameters, and a usage example.
## Technical Details — constraints, requirements, versions, dependencies.
The arrangement mirrors the logical structure of the thing described, so reader and subject can be navigated in parallel.
Describe and only describe. Neutral description is the imperative. No opinion, speculation, interpretation or marketing.
Adopt standard patterns. Put information where the reader expects it, in a format they recognize; consistency is what makes reference trustworthy.
Provide examples that illustrate usage without sliding into instruction or explanation.
Be austere and authoritative. Reference is consulted, not read through, so it must be unambiguous and complete enough to stand on.
Language: objective, present tense, precise. Avoid do this and follow these steps — link to a how-to instead.
Update the page when the thing it describes changes; a stale reference is worse than none.
Diataxis/Reference — the framework concept page this entity implements.

In this garden, Diataxis Tutorial pages model learning-oriented, hands-on lessons that take a beginner through meaningful practical steps. They guide learning and serve the acquisition of a skill, the studying quadrant of Diataxis.
Choosing between the four children, marking an instance, see-also:: and shared frontmatter follow Logseq/Entity/Diataxis.
A page whose job is to teach by doing: the reader ends it able to do something they could not do before, having produced a visible result along the way.

Not an instance: a page for someone who already knows the goal and needs the route — that is Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/How To. A page that describes or explains rather than teaches — Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/Reference or Logseq/Entity/Diataxis/Explanation.
[[Programming/Python/Tutorial/Build Your First Web App]] → pages/Programming___Python___Tutorial___Build Your First Web App.md.
tags:: — new pages of this kind carry [[Diataxis/Tutorial]] alongside their topic tags.
